summary: Replaced the 36 seeded research targets with the 8 real partners
body:
The seeded list (Swiss Re, Munich Re, Fermat, Dialog Axiata and the rest) was never contacted — every record sat at Identified with `seeded: true`. All 36 removed; git history keeps them. In their place: the real partner list, with stages taken from the status column — signed → MoU signed, send → MoU sent, need to be aligned → Researched.

Seventeen plan tasks pointed at deleted partners. Two Sri Lanka regulatory tasks (t303, t305) were repointed to the new Sri Lanka record; the other fifteen had their partner link cleared and need reattaching.

summary: Confirm the spelling and the signing entity
body: Entered as "Hakuhodo Key3" — the source list read "Hakahudo Key3", which looks like a typo for the Hakuhodo × Key3 joint venture. Confirm the spelling and the exact legal entity on the signed MoU.
"Sumitomo Insurance" is ambiguous — Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance (MS&AD) and Sumitomo Life are different houses with different appetites. Confirm which one holds the MoU before any follow-up goes out.

summary: Which Sumitomo entity runs the web3 activity?
body: Recorded as the digital-asset arm of the Sumitomo group. Confirm the entity name and whether it is the same counterparty as the insurance MoU or a separate one.

summary: "Sri Lanka" — which body is the counterparty?
body: Held as a single public-sector record for the host country. The alignment question is which body actually signs: the Insurance Regulatory Commission, the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission, the Central Bank, the Disaster Management Centre, or a ministry above them. Tasks t303 and t305 are attached here until that is settled — split the record once it is.
Write proxy is live. The desk now commits through it, so browsers hold a team password instead of a GitHub token; the token stays on the server.
